ayahs.1: A challenger has demanded a punishment bound to come
ayahs.2: for the those who reject the truth—none can avert it—
ayahs.3: from Allah, Lord of the pathways of ascent,
ayahs.4: by which the angels and the holy spirit ascend to Him on a Day whose length is fifty thousand years.
ayahs.5: So endure this denial, O Prophet, with beautiful sabr—steadfast endurance that keeps you upright.
ayahs.6: They see this Day as impossible,
ayahs.7: but We see it as inevitable.
ayahs.8: On that Day the sky will be like molten brass
ayahs.9: and the mountains like tufts of wool.
ayahs.10: No close friend will ask about their friends—
ayahs.11: though they will be made to see each other. The wicked will wish to ransom themselves from that Day's punishment with their children,
ayahs.12: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.13: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.15: and everyone on earth altogether—just to save themselves.
ayahs.16: But no! There will be a raging Flame
ayahs.17: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.18: It will summon whoever turned their backs on Allah and turned away from the truth,
ayahs.22: and withholding when touched with good—
ayahs.25: and who give the rightful share of their wealth to the beggar and the poor,
ayahs.26: and who firmly believe in the Day of Judgment,
ayahs.27: and those who fear the punishment of their Lord—
ayahs.28: knowing that none should feel secure from their Lord's punishment—
ayahs.29: and those who guard their chastity
ayahs.30: except with their spouses or those in their lawful possession, for then they are free from blame,
ayahs.31: but whoever seeks beyond that are the transgressors.
ayahs.32: They are also those true to their trusts and covenants,
ayahs.34: and properly observant of their salah.
ayahs.35: These will be in Gardens, held in honour.
ayahs.36: What is the matter with the those who reject the truth that they rush toward you, O Prophet,
ayahs.37: from right and left, in groups to mock you?
ayahs.38: Does each of them expect to be admitted into a Garden of Bliss?
ayahs.39: But no—they already know what We created them from.
ayahs.40: So I swear by the Lord of all points of sunrise and sunset that We are truly capable
ayahs.41: of replacing them with others better than them, and We cannot be prevented from doing so.
ayahs.42: So let them indulge in falsehood and amuse themselves until they face their Day, which they have been warned of—
ayahs.43: the Day they will come forth from the graves swiftly, as if racing to an idol,
ayahs.44: with eyes downcast, utterly covered in disgrace. That is the Day they have always been warned of.
